title: Bambu's H3C Is Here, $699 Toolchangers & AI-Designed Robots
subtitle: This week in 3D printing news

topics.title: Bambu H3C: $2,499, the First Bambu I'd Buy
topics.description: On sale since Tuesday. Nine preheated tools, a 9-spool AMS on top, and cheaper than a CORE One L INDX

slides.heading: Bambu H3C: $2,499, the First Bambu I'd Buy
slides.body: 247printing's 31-minute tech review, November 3. I don't usually love Bambu stuff, but this is the first Bambu printer I'd actually buy.

slides.heading: What You Get for $2,499
bullets: Sold only as a combo with the AMS 3H: $2,499, €2,499, £2,199. $2,589 with TPU 75A and a CMYKW PLA pack. $2,799 with the Bambu Station
Less than a Prusa CORE One L INDX, the closest match in size
Nine tools, each with its own heater and filament path. Bambu says a 6-second material swap and 0.038 g purge in its best case
330 × 320 × 325 mm. 350 °C nozzle, 120 °C bed, chamber heated to 65 °C
Takes 1.75 mm and 2.85 mm filament. The 2.85 mm tool is for TPU, down to 75A

slides.heading: What the Reviewers Found
bullets: AMS 3H holds nine spools, but only two slots dry, to 85 °C. Tom's Hardware and TechRadar: Editor's Choice. How-To Geek: 9/10
Tall: about a meter with the AMS on top, 36 kg. Reviewers reached for a step stool or the Bambu Station
CNC Kitchen, about 400 hours: 6–7 second swaps against about 40 on the H2C. Real prints only about 10% faster than an H2C or H2D
Each swap still primes about 50 mg. His Majora's Mask had over 4,000 swaps and about 200 g of waste
Mixed nozzle sizes in one print, each with its own layer height. Bambu Studio 2.9.1 has it now; reviewers say it still needs work

slides.heading: Meanwhile: Is the Prusa INDX Ready?
slides.body: 3D Printing Nerd, October 30. The hardware prints beautifully with very little waste. Getting files onto it is the hard part.

slides.heading: INDX: What Joel Found
bullets: Easy to unbox and load. Majora's Mask and Hellboy came out great
Filament management on the printer is "complex"
He switched between PrusaSlicer 2.9.6 and the 3.0 alpha and got firmware warnings on the latest firmware
Thomas Sanladerer called it "a tech demo at best." Joel won't go that far
Both he and CNC Kitchen say Bambu's software experience is ahead

topics.title: Black Friday: Four Toolchangers for Less
topics.description: Snapmaker U1 at $699, Flashforge Creator 5 at $599, the Creality K3 shipping at $849, and the H2C down to $1,899

slides.heading: Black Friday: Four Toolchangers for Less
bullets: Snapmaker U1: $699 for Black Friday, its lowest price yet. Four toolheads. Very affordable
Flashforge Creator 5: $599, down from $799, through November 30. The Creator 5 Pro is $749
Creality K3: $849. First orders shipped November 2, four free rolls of Hyper PLA through November 30. Tom's Hardware: "a tool changer, not a game changer"
Bambu H2C AMS Combo: $1,899 on sale, normally $2,199. Bambu's sale runs to December 1

topics.title: Slicer Week: Cura, Orca, Prusa and Bambu
topics.description: Every big slicer moved this week. Cura went stable today, Orca is one step from 2.5, and Prusa opened a plugin store

slides.heading: Slicer Week: Cura, Orca, Prusa and Bambu
bullets: Cura 5.14, stable today: paint supports on or off by hand, with an overhang-angle slider. Overhangs and bridges colored in the preview
OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 release candidate, November 1: Python plugins, belt printers, color mixing. The last test build before 2.5
OrcaSlicer has an official YouTube channel now

slides.heading: Prusa and Bambu Slicers
bullets: PrusaSlicer 3.0 alpha 13: a Lua plugin marketplace. Vase mode and soluble supports are now plugins
PrusaSlicer 2.9.7: security fixes for malformed 3MF and G-code files. Update
Bambu Studio 2.9.1: H3C support and mixed nozzle sizes. H2D gets it in November, H2C and X2D early 2027

topics.title: He Let 1,531 People Control His 3D Printer
topics.description: smill wrote a bot that printed the internet's most-liked model links for a week, unsupervised. Yikes

slides.heading: He Let 1,531 People Control His 3D Printer
slides.body: smill, October 28. Twelve minutes, almost 200,000 views. Whatever the internet sent went on his shelf.

slides.heading: How It Worked
bullets: People replied to his post with a model link. A bot queued them and printed the most-liked one next
A Bambu A1 Mini ran unsupervised for a week. He didn't look at anything until the end
Building his own slice-and-send pipeline took about two weeks
He worried someone could hide malicious instructions in a file. That's the yikes
Lesson: never auto-print files from strangers. Slice them yourself and keep your slicer updated

topics.title: Robotics Corner: TPU Legs and a Robot Dog
topics.description: University of Tokyo's printed TPU muscle legs, Mahdi Designs' $300 18-motor hand, Mishin Machine's tilting gear joint and Cubic Doggo

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: TPU Legs and a Robot Dog
slides.body: First up: robot legs with muscles, tendons and ligaments printed in TPU on a Prusa XL. University of Tokyo. No rigid joints, no bearings.

slides.heading: TPU Muscles: How It Works
bullets: Life-size legs, about 0.95 m. PLA bones, TPU 95A muscles, tendons and ligaments
Lattice thickness sets stiffness: 1.5 mm to 3 mm struts made one about 28 times stiffer
Motors at the pelvis pull six muscles through Bowden cables. Hip flexes about 90°, knee about 105°
Walks only with overhead support. One life-size muscle takes 20 to 40 hours to print
Published in Advanced Intelligent Systems, open access

slides.heading: A $300 Robot Hand With 18 Motors
slides.body: Mahdi Designs, November 3. A tendon-driven humanoid hand from printed parts and cheap servos. Still in development.

slides.heading: A Gear Joint That Tilts 180°
slides.body: Mishin Machine, mid-October. Trochoidal teeth stay in mesh through a 180° tilt. Resin printed on a Form 4, driven by a CubeMars motor.

slides.heading: Grok Bot's Pick: Cubic Doggo 07B Wouf
Cubic Doggo: What Goes Into It
bullets: A printable 12-servo robot dog on the same ST-3215 servos as the SO-101 arm. 2.2 kg, walks carrying over 1 kg
PLA+ body, 12 ST-3215 servos on two Waveshare bus boards
Raspberry Pi 5 running ROS 2 Jazzy, joystick control
No custom PCB, only two solder joints. M3 screws and locknuts, no glue
Editable FreeCAD files on GitHub and Printables
Servo screws must be exactly 10 mm. One millimeter too long can damage a servo

topics.title: AI Corner: An AI-Designed Dancing Pumpkin
topics.description: One plain-English prompt, no manual CAD. AI agents designed and simulated a 12-joint robot, and the team printed it

slides.heading: AI Corner: An AI-Designed Dancing Pumpkin
slides.body: Google DeepMind, Halloween. AI agents designed, simulated and helped build this robot from one plain-English prompt.

slides.heading: The Pumpkin: What We Know
bullets: 12 degrees of freedom. No manual CAD
Agents ran on Gemini 4 Argon in Google's Antigravity
3D printed, with off-the-shelf actuators, a Raspberry Pi and a servo controller. Parts many of us already own
No files yet. The team hopes to publish a tech report and maybe the design. Battery safety held it back

bullets: Fit spheres, cylinders and planes to a scan, then measure between them

Map wall thickness
